audit.whatIsWrong: Bear Trap on a Rope was described only as 'Projectile hook — Wind Wall blocks it!' with no cooldown, and the page never said what Violent Tendencies actually does.
audit.why: Bear Trap is 800 range on 11/10/9/8/7s; Wind Wall is 25s at rank 1 falling to 17s, so you cannot wall every hook — the cooldown gap is the real advice. Violent Tendencies (W) grants four fast attacks with a bigger fourth (autoReset flag): the attack-speed burst is the tell to disengage.
audit.corrected: Named the 11s rank-1 hook against Wind Wall's 25s, and wrote the Violent Tendencies four-attack pattern into the don'ts.

audit.whatIsWrong: Levels 4-5 and 6 were marked Skill and 2+ items was given to Kled — against the packet chart, the mirror, and this page's own prose.
audit.why: The mirror flipped 4-5 and 6 to Kled and 2+ items to Yasuo. The content layer already said 'Late game flips to you' at whys[6] while win[6] said Kled — the page contradicted itself.
audit.corrected: Rows: Skill, Kled, Kled, Kled, Kled, Kled, Yasuo — matched full/content pairs.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why and phases[6].why were boilerplate with no Kled content.
audit.why: Chaaaaaaaarge!! is 140s at rank 1 and carries a shield — meeting it head-on is the classic loss. The two-item window matters because dismounted Kled has no mount health to hide behind.
audit.corrected: Both rewritten to the real cooldown and the dismount condition.

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemization recommended Executioner's Calling 'early — his healing fights your pattern', and breakdown.late said 'anti-heal stays core'.
audit.why: Kled has no healing in his kit. His passive restores Skaarl's courage to remount; that is not healing and Grievous Wounds does not touch it. Buying anti-heal here is wasted gold. The mirror flagged the identical error in the other direction.
audit.corrected: Replaced with Plated Steelcaps reasoning against his physical damage and an explicit 'skip Grievous Wounds'.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on how the two displacements interact.
audit.why: Last Breath only blinks to an AIRBORNE target. Riot's text for Bear Trap says the target is 'yanked toward Kled' — a pull, not an airborne state — so the derived knockup flag on his Q contradicts the description. Your own Steel Tempest whirlwind is the only knockup in the lane that sets up your R.
audit.corrected: Stated in report[5].t; flagged the flag/description conflict for the maintainer.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Bear Trap on a Rope's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: His Bear Trap is down to 8s while Wind Wall is 19s — you cannot wall them all. Farm safe and take only the baited-hook trades.

edits.before: Last Breath converts ANY knockup into a kill window. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Kled's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Chaaaaaaaarge!! is 140s at rank 1 and hands him a shield plus engage — do not meet it head-on, fight after he spends it.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Kled carry threat 7/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items on: crit plus Last Breath bursts the dismounted Kled before Skaarl's courage refills. Force the side lane now.

edits.before: Projectile hook — Wind Wall blocks it! Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: An 800-range projectile on 11s at rank 1 — Wind Wall eats it; step up in the gap.

edits.before: Kled wastes Bear Trap on a Rope — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Chip Skaarl's health bar down, then all-in the fragile dismounted Kled.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: He rebuilds Skaarl's courage by fighting — disengage once dismounted.

edits.before: Dashing INTO his engage with passive shield down — the wave is your armor; off it you are the squishiest melee alive.
edits.after: Violent Tendencies gives him four fast attacks with a big fourth — walk away when the attack speed spikes, not after it.

edits.before: Track Kled's Bear Trap on a Rope: Projectile hook — Wind Wall blocks it! When it is down — EQ-R him.
edits.after: Bear Trap is a projectile Wind Wall eats, 11s at rank 1. Riot's text yanks you to him — no knockup.

edits.before: Start Doran's Blade + pot. Core: Blade of the Ruined King  (duel spike), then Infinity Edge; boots Plated Steelcaps. Executioner's Calling early — his healing fights your pattern.
edits.after: Start Doran's Blade + pot. Core: Blade of the Ruined King, then Infinity Edge; boots Plated Steelcaps against his physical W. Kled has no healing — skip Grievous Wounds here.

edits.before: Last Breath converts ANY knockup into a kill window — build your teamfight around that. Kled carry threat: 7/10 — anti-heal stays core, shift to picks and wave control if he gets ahead.
edits.after: Last Breath converts ANY knockup into a kill window — build your teamfight around that. Kled carry threat: 7/10 — dismounted he is fragile, so force the fight after Skaarl breaks.

notes: Two substantive fixes: the anti-heal recommendation was against a champion with no healing (Skaarl's courage is not a heal), and win[6] said Kled while whys[6] on the same page said the late game flips to Yasuo. For the maintainer: Kled's Q has a derived 'knockup' flag but Riot's own description says the target is 'yanked toward Kled' — a pull, not an airborne state. Per the brief's rule I trusted the description. That matters because Last Breath needs an AIRBORNE target, so if the flag is right somewhere else in the repo, Yasuo pages may be promising an R entry that does not exist.
